subject: QPS & token-frame clarity — post-call follow-up and next actions
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@cloudbridge.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@cloudbridge.io
Date: 2026-09-05T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: performance & SLO details

Thanks for the call earlier — quick note to capture our current understanding and a couple of clarifying questions so your sizing can be tighter. Attaching a small sample (sample_traffic.csv) and a short session trace (session_trace.json).

Current product notes (from our ops telemetry):
- Avg tokens per user request: ~200 tokens
- Typical peak single-request size: up to ~1,200 tokens (rare, p99-ish)
- Steady-state QPS: ~5 requests/sec globally
- Peak burst QPS observed during launches: ~120 req/sec for ~5-15 minutes
- ~18% of requests are streamed (server-sent partial tokens for realtime suggestions)

Latency targets we care about (what we told product):
- Non-streaming p95: < 300 ms (soft target), p99: prefer < 500 ms
- Streaming: initial partial token ideally < 150 ms; subsequent token cadence as low as possible

Questions for Redwood to confirm in sizing:
1) How do you map these inputs to capacity (tokens/sec -> GPU pools) assuming quantized model variants?
2) For streaming requests, how does concurrency (open sessions) affect effective qps and KV cache pressure?
3) What telemetry fields do you need from us to validate the canary?

Next steps: can you come back with an initial sizing estimate + proposed canary cadence? We can be available 9/9 for a follow-up.

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Head of Platform Engineering — CloudBridge
samir@cloudbridge.io
Attachments: sample_traffic.csv (csv), session_trace.json (json)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@cloudbridge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-05T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance & SLO details

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and files. Quick read-through and a short list of assumptions Im making for the initial sizing exercise. I attached a short note were putting together (initial-sizing-notes.pdf).

Key Redwood assumptions for the draft estimate:
- Avg tokens/call = 200 (unless you provide a tighter distribution)
- Steady-state qps = 5; short bursts to 120 qps for <20 minutes
- Streaming calls maintain an open connection; we assume 18% concurrency fraction
- Target SLOs: well optimize for p95 latency on the non-streaming path and initial-byte latency on streaming

Clarifying requests from our side (quick answers will materially change the estimate):
- Can you share p50/p90/p99 token-size distribution (or confirm the attached sample is representative)?
- Fraction of calls that are idempotent vs. stateful (affects cache effectiveness)?
- Are there geographically-localized hot spots (e.g., 60% traffic from a single region)?

Planned deliverables and timeline:
- By EOD 9/6: initial-sizing-notes.pdf (ballpark GPU sizing, batch vs streaming config trade-offs, KV cache recommendations)
- By 9/8: a small model/sim run with your sample to sanity-check latency projections
- Follow-up call: Wed 2026-09-09 10:00 PT (please confirm)

If that schedule works, well also add Marissa for the detailed throughput mapping and loop Neha for telemetry fields.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachments: initial-sizing-notes.pdf (summary)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@cloudbridge.io>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-06T11:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance & SLO details

On Sep 5, 2026, Vivek Kulkarni wrote:
> Samir  thanks for the clear summary and files. Quick read-through and a short list of assumptions Im making for the initial sizing exercise.

Folks  following up with a concrete throughput breakdown and an operational playbook we recommend for the canary. High level first, then action items.

Throughput / token math (ballpark):
- Steady-state tokens/sec = steady_qps * avg_tokens = 5 qps * 200 tokens = ~1,000 tokens/sec
- Typical peak window (morning release): peak_qps ~45 for ~30-45 minutes -> tokens/sec = 45 * 200 = 9,000 t/s
- Burst spikes (launch events) = 120 qps * up to 1,200 tokens = ~144,000 t/s (short duration, need fast autoscale)

Concurrency & streaming notes:
- Streaming sessions keep RAM and KV-cache resources reserved per open connection; plan for ~1.8x effective concurrency headroom for streaming-heavy windows
- Prefetch/warm KV cache policy reduces first-request latency for repeated prefixes; warmup window of 10-20 minutes recommended before increasing traffic to a new canary cohort

Suggested SLO mapping (proposed for discussion):
- Non-streaming: p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 450 ms
- Streaming initial token: p50 <= 80 ms, p95 <= 220 ms

Operational canary proposal:
- Phase 1: 3% traffic for 24 hours (validate correctness & basic latency)
- Phase 2: 10% traffic for 48 hours with KV-cache warmup (validate tail and throughput)
- Phase 3: ramp to 50% over 24 hours, smoke test autoscale under synthetic spikes

Telemetry fields we need (Neha to own):
- request_id, timestamp, routing_region, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant, streaming_flag, client_latency_ms, backend_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit

Action items:
- Neha: share telemetry ingestion spec + sample query that returns p50/p95/p99 by window (due 9/08)
- Samir: confirm whether release spikes are predictable (cron-based) or ad-hoc (affects autoscale)
- Vivek/Marissa: deliver sizing spreadsheet and canary playbook (9/08)

Happy to walk through the spreadsheet on the 9/9 call.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Samir Rao <samir@cloudbridge.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-07T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance & SLO details

Thanks — that all looks reasonable. A few concrete datapoints from our side (attached traffic_windows.csv):
- Steady window (local daytime): 00:00-20:00 UTC equivalent -> ~5 qps sustained
- Morning peak: 08:00-09:00 local -> ~45 qps for 30-45 mins
- Release spikes: ~3x baseline, last ~10-15 minutes, somewhat unpredictable (we often see them after deploys)
- Token distribution (rough): p50=180, p90=620, p99=1,150
- Streaming fraction: ~18% of requests; streaming sessions last on average ~9s

Were aligned on the canary plan: start 9/09 10:00 PT with Phase 1 at 3%. Ill share pager contacts and the deploy schedule before the call. Attached traffic_windows.csv.

Samir Rao
Head of Platform Engineering — CloudBridge
samir@cloudbridge.io
